corpus.name: Public-Domain Modern Cursive Hebrew Manuscripts (HeOCR/hash PDM-1.0)
corpus.description: Six public-domain (PDM-1.0) handwritten cursive Hebrew manuscript pages (1892-1930) by Rachel Bluwstein, H. N. Bialik, and N. H. Imber, with independently reviewed public-domain transcripts from Wikisource / HeOCR/hash. Includes graph-ruled notebook paper, wide-spaced short notes, faint low-DPI ink, and authorial cross-outs. Distinct from contemporary school notebooks (kept in benchmark/modern_school pending school consent), and distinct from early-modern 1500-1800 Pinkas records.

pages.notes: Modern Hebrew cursive ink manuscript (1930) on unruled paper; verbatim public-domain diplomatic/Wikisource transcript from HeOCR/hash.
4-line wide-spaced cursive ink manuscript (1892) with vocalization marks; tests pitch estimation on short notes with wide line spacing (>15% page height).
Autograph Hebrew cursive stanza, chorus, and author signature (1907-1908) on unruled paper.

1928 cursive draft containing authorial strike-throughs and interlinear revisions; upstream reference carries the final intended reading, providing a realistic lower-bound stress test for crossed-out draft lines.
High-resolution photograph (3456x5184 EXIF-oriented) on graph-ruled notebook paper (נייר משובץ) with archival shelfmark top-left and Gnazim stamp bottom-right.
Low-resolution scan (370x550) of thin/faint cursive strokes on aged notebook paper; tests thin-stroke binarization without morphological stroke erasure.

note: the pages that were measured have a transcript that was checked by somebody who is not the one who wrote it down
